description: Hand-picked question -> expected-verse pairs for evaluating retrieval accuracy. Expand this as the corpus grows; each entry's expected_verses should be verses a knowledgeable reader would agree directly address the question.

cases.question: What happens to the soul when the body dies?
Who is the true enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices?
Show me Krishna's universal form with many faces and eyes.
I freeze up before a hard decision -- my hands shake, my mind goes blank, I can't function. What does Krishna show us through Arjuna in this moment?
As someone others look up to (at work, at home), how much does my own behavior actually shape the people around me?
I've made serious mistakes in my past and feel unworthy. Is there really a way back?
How do I stop being ruled by my anger and cravings? Is real happiness even possible while they're this strong?
I keep overdoing everything -- work, food, even rest. What does the Gita say about finding balance?
I only think of God when I'm in trouble. Is that a weak or unworthy kind of faith?
I want to feel God's presence in daily life, not just in a crisis. How do I actually stay connected?
I feel lost and confused about which way to go in life. Where does real clarity come from?
How do I stop being so reactive -- to criticism, to people who upset me -- and find real inner steadiness?
I don't feel spiritually advanced or wise myself. Is it enough to simply listen to and trust those who are?
My moods swing so much with what's happening around me. How do I stop being at their mercy?
I know exactly what's holding me back -- old attachments -- but I can't seem to cut free. What does Krishna say to do?
What are the real root causes of self-destructive behavior, and how do I actually get free of them?
Does what I eat and how I live really affect my mind and spirit, according to the Gita?
I'm exhausted trying to do everything 'right.' Is there a final, simplest refuge Krishna offers?
